title: The Sakakibara Health Integrative Profile Cohort Study
brief_summary: Because of the genetic and traditional commonalities between the underlying causes of atherosclerotic cardiovascular diseases (CVD) and cancers, we hypothesized that patients with atherosclerotic CVD may have a high incidence of cancers when compared with those with non-atherosclerotic CVD. To address this hypothesis, we investigated longitudinal clinical outcomes in a total of 32,095 consecutive patients with CVD enrolled in the Sakakibara Health Integrative Profile (SHIP) cohort study which was launched in 2006 for the purpose of improving healthy life expectancy in patients with CVD in our institute.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Among a total of 36,151 patients with any CVD enrolled in the SHIP cohort study between June 2006 and July 2014, we analyzed a total of 32,095 consecutive patients with acquired CVD in the present study after excluding 4,056 patients with known cancers and/or congenital CVD.

Exclusion Criteria:

* We excluded 245 patients who had already been diagnosed with any cancers at the time of enrollment in the SHIP cohort study, and 3,811 patients with congenital CVD including Marfan syndrome.
study_population: A total of 36,151 patients (58% male, 61±23 years) with any cardiovascular diseases (CVD) enrolled in the SHIP cohort study between June 2006 and July 2014.
